title: Getting Started with lstparsR
text: lstparsR reads NONMEM .lst listing files extracts parameter estimates tidy tibbles. designed population pharmacokinetic pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) workflows many model runs need parsed programmatically. Key design choices: Parameter output returned tibbles consistent column names. Missing optional quantities (e.g., standard errors covariance step absent) NA. Missing required parameter sections raise errors; fetch_all() catches , warns, returns NULL failed elements. VECTOR blocks (THETA) lower-triangular MATRIX blocks (OMEGA, SIGMA) handled, including multi-line parameter sets.

title: Getting Started with lstparsR
text: Use read_lst_file() load .lst file S3 object class "lst". examples use synthetic listings ship package (see Synthetic Example Listings); one FOCE-run complete covariance step: lst object simply character vector (one element per line) class "lst" attached. fetch_* functions require class.
code: path <- system.file("extdata", "lst", "s01_focei_cov_success.lst",                     package = "lstparsR") lst  <- read_lst_file(path) lst #> <lst> NONMEM listing file: 456 lines summary(lst) #> <lst> NONMEM listing file #>   Lines            : 456 #>   Estimation method: FIRST ORDER CONDITIONAL ESTIMATION WITH INTERACTION #>   Covariance step  : TRUE

title: Getting Started with lstparsR

title: Getting Started with lstparsR
text: package ships 39 small, invented listings extdata/lst, generated script (data-raw/make_synthetic_lst.R source repository). case exercises one estimation method, run outcome layout feature, successful FOCE-run complete covariance step aborted covariance steps, chained $ESTIMATION records, wrapped parameter records truncated files. manifest.csv describes cases values contain: Parsing side side shows unavailable quantities reported: standard errors condition number become NA covariance step aborted reached, fetch_all() returns NULL parameter tables truncated listing contain.
code: corpus   <- system.file("extdata", "lst", package = "lstparsR") manifest <- read.csv(file.path(corpus, "manifest.csv")) head(manifest[, c("case_id", "final_method", "covariance")]) #>   case_id                                        final_method    covariance #> 1     s01 First Order Conditional Estimation with Interaction     completed #> 2     s02                  First Order Conditional Estimation     completed #> 3     s03                                         First Order     completed #> 4     s04   Laplacian Conditional Estimation with Interaction     completed #> 5     s05                                 Iterative Two Stage not requested #> 6     s06   Stochastic Approximation Expectation-Maximization     completed cases <- c("s01", "s09", "s15", "s18", "s32") files <- file.path(corpus, manifest$file[match(cases, manifest$case_id)]) runs  <- lapply(files, function(f) suppressWarnings(fetch_all(read_lst_file(f)))) data.frame(   case       = cases,   covariance = manifest$covariance[match(cases, manifest$case_id)],   thetas     = vapply(runs, function(r) NROW(r$thetas), integer(1)),   se_th1     = vapply(runs, function(r) if (is.null(r$thetas)) NA else r$thetas$se[1], numeric(1)),   ofv        = vapply(runs, function(r) r$ofv, numeric(1)),   condn      = round(vapply(runs, function(r) r$condn, numeric(1)), 2) ) #>   case                 covariance thetas se_th1       ofv condn #> 1  s01                  completed      4  0.312  1873.406  3.17 #> 2  s09      from posterior sample      2  0.238 -2187.645  6.81 #> 3  s15                    aborted      4     NA  1885.071    NA #> 4  s18 completed (no eigenvalues)      4  0.329  1871.952    NA #> 5  s32                interrupted      0     NA  1874.109    NA

title: lstparsR: Tidy Parsing of NONMEM Listing Files
text: Population pharmacokinetic pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) modeling NONMEM produces listing files (.lst) contain parameter estimates, standard errors, objective function values, eigenvalues, shrinkage statistics structured complex text format. Extracting quantities downstream analysis — model comparison tables, forest plots, covariate analyses — typically requires manual copy-paste ad-hoc scripts fragile error-prone. lstparsR provides clean, validated interface reading .lst files returning tidy data frames. designed two goals: Robustness. Parsers return NA unavailable optional quantities. Missing required parameter sections raise errors. batch workflows, fetch_all() catches individual parser errors, warns, returns NULL elements retaining results. Tidiness. Parameter output returned tibbles consistent, lowercase column names (parameter, estimate, se, rse, shrinkage) ready binding across runs dplyr purrr. package recognizes FO, FOCE, FOCE-, LAPLACE, , SAEM, IMP, IMPMAP BAYES method headers. Output layout coverage described .

what: lstparsR: Tidy Parsing of 'NONMEM' Listing Files — lstparsR-package
title: lstparsR: Tidy Parsing of 'NONMEM' Listing Files — lstparsR-package
text: Extracts parameter estimates diagnostics 'NONMEM' listing files population pharmacokinetic pharmacodynamic analyses. Returns fixed-effect estimates, random-effect variance diagonals, standard errors, relative standard errors, objective function values, eigenvalue-based condition numbers, shrinkage tidy tables scalar values. Missing optional quantities represented NA; combined parser preserves partial results individual sections parsed. optional 'shiny' application supports file uploads table downloads. Parsing existing listing files require 'NONMEM' installation.

title: lstparsR: Tidy Parsing of 'NONMEM' Listing Files — lstparsR-package
text: Parsers use final problem estimation step. Explicit #PROB: #METH: markers delimit results; legacy listings use final result pages. failed final step reuse earlier estimates covariance output.

title: lstparsR 0.1.0
text: Initial development release. read_lst_file(): reads NONMEM .lst files; returns S3 class "lst". fetch_thetas(): THETA estimates SE RSE. fetch_etas(): OMEGA diagonal SE, RSE, ETA shrinkage. fetch_sigmas(): SIGMA diagonal SE RSE. fetch_ofv(): objective function value fallback workflow footer. fetch_condn(): condition number eigenvalues. fetch_all(): convenience wrapper returning . run_app(): interactive Shiny application uploading, viewing, downloading parsed results. Recognizes FOCE-, FOCE, FO, SAEM, IMP, IMPMAP, Bayesian method headers. Handles multi-line parameter blocks (>12 THETAs spanning multiple rows). Missing optional covariance quantities returned NA. Exercised 7,600 listing files, predominantly FOCE-.
